html:
A 1976 book by the American writer Alex Haley, who traced his family back to Kunta Kinte, a young Mandinka man he said was taken from the village of Juffureh on the Gambia River and enslaved in Virginia.

The book and its 1977 television series reached tens of millions of people and changed how Americans spoke about slavery and African roots. Historians have questioned parts of Haley's genealogy. For the Gambia it made Juffureh and James Island places of pilgrimage for the African diaspora, and they became the core of the country's tourism. The slave trade story it told had long been absent from schoolbooks.
